author: Codex socialist_green assessment agent (AI-assisted independent assessment)
changeNote: Completed 240 individually interpreted responses and separate substantive evidence review. User authorised neutral representative doctrinal modelling; no 12Axes answers or scores imported.

metadata.name: Luxemburgism
metadata.description: Luxemburg’s democratic revolutionary Marxism, combining mass participation, political freedom, social ownership and international solidarity.
metadata.scope: Luxemburg’s democratic, mass-participatory revolutionary Marxism, reconstructed from her writings and scholarship. The profile preserves her rejection of narrow nationalism and bureaucratic substitution for workers’ action. It does not attribute contemporary government conduct or the policies of later parties to her. This is a representative interpretation, not a questionnaire submitted by adherents. Numeric neutral means a stated mixed/conditional judgement, including rejection of the premise where explained; it is not a claim of measured empirical equivalence. Modern biological and technology items are conditional interpretive judgements where no exact historical position exists; they must not be read as empirical findings or a representative survey of adherents.
metadata.phrase: A socialist society developed through workers’ mass participation, political freedom and international solidarity.

sources.title: Muldoon and Booth: Socialist democracy: Rosa Luxemburg’s challenge to democratic theory
Critique of the Gotha Programme, Part I (1875)
Theses on Feuerbach (1845; Engels edited edition)

axes.brief: Luxemburg insists on elections, press freedom, open debate and mass participation against Bolshevik political exclusion.
axes.counterEvidence: Her support for revolution and proletarian power does not erase her explicit criticism of replacing general elections with a party clique. The SAGE reconstruction is an interpretation, not her own complete constitution.

answers.rationale: General elections are explicitly necessary for living socialist institutions.
A few intellectuals cannot substitute their judgement for mass political experience.
Her defence of women’s suffrage and broad participation supports universal adult voting.
Rule by decree suppresses the public learning socialism needs.
Freedom specifically includes political opponents.
Public control is necessary to prevent corruption.
Independent rights checks fit her anti-clique argument, though no exact judicial blueprint is supplied.
Union or party elites cannot replace the whole population’s political action.
Privileging one party destroys freedom’s substance.
Direct mass participation supports binding popular decisions with freedom safeguards.
A handful of leaders cannot administer socialism for passive spectators.
Public accountability supports removal of abusive officials.
Postponing representative congresses is itself criticised as clique rule.
Recall can keep representatives subject to active popular control.
Unaccountable power extinguishes living public institutions.
Military substitution for popular power contradicts workers’ self-emancipation.

axes.brief: Political freedom and mass initiative are indispensable to socialism, while revolutionary measures against property remain legitimate.
axes.counterEvidence: She accepts force against property, but expressly criticises terror and draconian penalties as politically demoralising.

answers.rationale: Personal freedom weighs against punishing self-regarding choices.
Serious-harm prevention can justify limited inquiry but surveillance risks suppressing dissent.
Assembly and mass strikes are central political rights.
Unrestricted criticism is essential to public learning.
Common health and personal liberty require public deliberation, not a doctrinally fixed command.
Long-term indiscriminate tracking threatens mass political freedom.
Road-harm prevention is legitimate but routine police compulsion needs democratic justification.
Pre-offence restraint risks the arbitrary repression she condemns.
Freedom of opinion includes material disliked by authorities.
Political organising should not require state identification permission.
Suspicionless search risks using public order against popular action.
Predicted disorder is easily used to extinguish assembly.
Warrants constrain the arbitrary force she criticises.
Disclosure of wrongdoing enables the public control she demands.
Popular revolutionary defence supports civilian defensive capacity.
Indefinite court-free detention resembles the terror politics she rejects.

axes.brief: Anti-racism and opposition to colonial cultural destruction accompany international class solidarity.
axes.counterEvidence: Her rejection of nationalism differs from hostility to ethnic rights. SEP records attention to Indigenous communal ownership and colonial violence.

answers.rationale: Anti-colonial solidarity rejects national cultural supremacy.
Equal participation can warrant practical cultural accommodation.
Workers’ solidarity should not demand cultural conversion.
International solidarity includes people with distinct identities.
Shared communication matters but dominant-language exclusion harms participation.
Recognition respects communities whose cultures colonialism destroys.
Cultural support should not automatically privilege the majority tradition.
Neither nationalist uniformity nor sectional separatism should override common emancipation.
Plural observances can coexist within common public life.
Diverse histories can belong to the shared political community.
Wider political participation matters without requiring cultural erasure.
Language access helps excluded workers join common public life.
A nation-first family identity can reinforce divisions among workers.
Cultural freedom and equal public rules require contextual judgement on a special exemption.
Anti-racism supports a common society with distinct ways of life.
Shared organising need not require adopting majority customs.

axes.brief: International solidarity and critique of dispossession support migrant inclusion; administrative visa instruments are reasoned modern applications.
axes.counterEvidence: No incumbent state is assigned as a Luxemburgist representative. These are doctrinal inferences, not fabricated historical votes on visa categories.

answers.rationale: Rigid national quotas conflict with international solidarity.
Migration for better life fits solidarity across borders.
Selecting only useful skills treats people as instruments of capital.
Family unity deserves protection across national boundaries.
Refugee protection should not depend on cultural fit.
Anti-exclusion supports regularisation, while individual circumstances still matter.
Native-worker exclusion does not resolve capitalist labour competition.
Housing investment and admission management need democratic assessment rather than automatic reduction.
Family rights should not be mechanically subordinated to a common quota.
Employment can justify admission without exhausting legitimate migration grounds.
Independent movement should not depend entirely on sponsorship.
Education is a meaningful connection but not a universal settlement guarantee.
International solidarity supports refuge beyond ordinary numerical ceilings.
Preference by cultural origin reproduces national hierarchy.
Equal social provision should include migrant workers and families.
Cultural difference can enrich life but is not a superior admission entitlement.

axes.brief: Opposition to imperial war and war credits coexists with support for workers’ revolution and resistance.
axes.counterEvidence: Revolutionary commitment means that peace at all costs would be inaccurate despite opposition to imperial militarism.

answers.rationale: Competitive national interests do not justify military aggression.
Antiwar internationalism prioritises negotiation.
Competitive military superiority sustains the imperial system she opposes.
Genuine imminent defence differs from imperial war, but preemption requires exceptional scrutiny.
Revolutionary liberation is not confined to defending an existing state or ally.
Militarising male citizens for national rivalry conflicts with internationalist organising.
Avoiding workers killing workers can justify major concessions.
Delegating killing to autonomous systems contradicts active human responsibility.
Defensive popular protection is preferable to imperial campaigns.
Revolutionary commitment rules out avoiding every armed struggle.
Long expeditionary campaigns are characteristic of imperial militarism.
Territorial nationalism should not cause another war.
Military coercion for concessions perpetuates imperial rivalry.
War prevention outweighs nationalist resolve.
Escalatory state espionage generally serves competitive militarism.
Negotiated reductions can weaken the machinery of imperial war.

axes.brief: Luxemburg rejects national self-determination as a sufficient emancipation strategy and prioritises transnational working-class organisation.
axes.counterEvidence: International worker organisation is not equivalent to obedience to every existing international institution or capitalist court.

answers.rationale: National supremacy is not an end of workers’ emancipation.
Transnational democracy is supported but existing institutions may reproduce capitalist domination.
Neither national nor international courts are entitled to class-blind finality.
International solidarity requires organisation, not automatic allegiance to military blocs.
Freedom from imperial commitments can advance workers’ autonomy.
International accountability matters, but the institution’s political character remains decisive.
International workers’ interests outrank national prestige and advantage.
Shared environmental problems justify international democratic coordination.
Common international policy can help, whereas bourgeois bloc discipline can obstruct solidarity.
International safeguards for civil freedom can support emancipation if democratically accountable.
Currency scale is conditional on workers’ control and social needs.
Shared decisions and resources embody practical international solidarity.
National border sovereignty should not be absolute against human solidarity.
Common trade rules are useful only if they do not entrench exploitation.

International working-class association is favoured, but national democratic institutions can remain during transformation; support depends on the proposed federation’s class character and accountability.
Collective action should serve emancipation rather than enforce imperial rules indiscriminately.

axes.brief: Social ownership and democratic economic control replace private capitalist power; bureaucracy alone cannot create socialism.
axes.counterEvidence: SAGE argues for public ownership plus plural institutions, but Luxemburg’s own text stresses that socialist institutions cannot be decreed by a few officials.

answers.rationale: Private capital’s domination must be replaced by social control.
Common utilities fit democratic public ownership.
Democratic economic power matters beyond equal short-run service metrics.
Socialist ownership extends to productive sectors beyond natural monopolies.
Health provision should be democratically controlled rather than privately appropriated.
Collective transport infrastructure is suitable for public ownership.
Lower cost alone does not justify private class control of services.
Public finance can advance social direction during transition.
Selling collective productive resources reverses the socialist objective.
Public housing can secure collective needs and reduce landlord domination.
Regulation alone leaves strategic class power in private hands.
Collective resource control can resist extractive capitalist dispossession.
Publicly controlled delivery is preferred to routine capitalist contracting.
Strategic social ownership should not be exchanged merely for sale revenue.
Democratic reform of a service should be considered before privatisation.
Public broadcasting is acceptable with pluralism and opposition freedom.

axes.brief: International accumulation is criticised for coercion and dependency; neither domestic capital nor unrestricted global capital receives automatic preference.
axes.counterEvidence: Her analysis of imperial economic coercion limits any inference that global integration is automatically emancipatory.

answers.rationale: National capitalist protection and unrestricted global exploitation are both inadequate.
Removing barriers can widen cooperation but may deepen dependency.
Worker and community benefit matters more than supplier nationality alone.
Global sourcing must be judged against dispossession and labour conditions.
Resilience can help workers while national autarky can divide them.
Unilateral openness has no universal virtue independent of social consequences.
Infant-industry protection can develop productive forces or strengthen domestic exploitation.
Foreign and domestic capital should face democratic social controls alike.
Food security and the interests of workers abroad require contextual balance.
Workers should not be abandoned to destructive global adjustment.
Retaliatory tariffs can reinforce competing national capitalist blocs.
Equal ordinary taxes avoid arbitrary national discrimination.
Foreign subsidies are not objectionable merely for being foreign.
Trade rules should not deepen dependency without protecting popular control.
Preventing strategic dispossession may justify blocking foreign control.
Cross-border access to useful services can support international connection.

axes.brief: Democratic social planning is supported, while the form of socialist production must develop through mass experience rather than a fixed party blueprint.
axes.counterEvidence: The Russian Revolution explicitly denies that detailed socialist institutions can be specified in advance; conditional responses preserve this anti-dogmatism.

answers.rationale: Production should be socially directed rather than independently governed by capital.
Democratic production targets can coordinate needs without dictatorial factory discipline.
Social needs should qualify market price allocation.
Democratic planning should guide common investment.
Solvent demand alone cannot decide workers’ and communities’ future.
Essential-price regulation can support material emancipation.
Strategic production should answer to common democratic priorities.
Credit should support democratically chosen social production.
Capital flight should not veto collective economic change.
Democratic investment can redirect development beyond private profitability.
Private currency rivalry would reinforce unaccountable financial power.
Immediate worker protections are worthwhile within a revolutionary strategy.
Workers’ active negotiation is preferable to decrees from isolated officials.
Monetary tools should serve democratic social planning.
Housing need should constrain market rent extraction.
Democratic common coordination should replace capitalist production anarchy.

axes.brief: Working-class emancipation supports substantial social provision and redistribution but ultimately changes ownership rather than only transfers.
axes.counterEvidence: Her critique of reformism does not mean rejecting immediate material gains. The distinction concerns whether reforms replace the emancipatory objective.

answers.rationale: Substantial transfers can reduce workers’ insecurity while ownership changes proceed.
Reducing class inequality is a legitimate fiscal objective.
A strong minimum supports participation in public life.
Mere subsistence does not constitute social emancipation.
Graduated contributions can challenge concentrated class advantage.
Greater retention at the top should not outweigh workers’ social needs.
Inherited class advantage can legitimately fund common support.
Ongoing deprivation should not be excused by a benefit time limit.
Wealth transfers can counter concentrated class resources.
Taxpayer convenience should not dictate impoverished benefit levels.
Participation in common social life is essential to active citizenship.
Tax reductions do not generally outrank expanding inadequate provision.
Supplements can aid workers, though they do not replace workplace power.
Equal marginal tax rates ignore unequal class resources.
Common land control is preferred; compensated subdivision is a conditional reform.
Broad social provision should extend beyond households at survival risk.

axes.brief: Political freedom and Marxist social explanation oppose privileged clerical rule while protecting freedom of opinion.
axes.counterEvidence: The cited political-freedom argument supports private conscience; her secular Marxist analysis is not evidence for religious persecution.

answers.rationale: Civil collective decisions should not rest on religious revelation.
Clerical teaching cannot bind a politically free socialist public.
Government should be accountable to people rather than religious approval.
An official foundation in one faith conflicts with equal political participation.
Open study should enable independent judgement rather than conversion.
State faith instruction restricts free intellectual development.
Secular civil institutions should determine enforceable law.
Religious leaders should not receive a privileged legislative gatekeeping role.
Inclusive public ceremonies should avoid compulsory religious endorsement.
Public resources should serve common needs rather than creed promotion.
Equal civic status supports avoiding official religious symbols.
Cultural festivals may persist without official religious privilege.
Clerical status cannot substitute for democratic accountability.
Faith organisations should not receive privileges beyond common charitable rules.
Marriage decisions should be free of clerical permission.
Religious family jurisdiction risks subordinating free and equal individuals.

axes.brief: Women’s emancipation challenges household and workplace oppression; modern identity questions remain cautious applications.
axes.counterEvidence: SEP documents both active support for women’s suffrage and criticism of class-exclusive feminism. Neither implies a fully specified present-day sexual ethics.

answers.rationale: Emancipation requires the ability to transform inherited social relations.
Established practices cannot outrank freedom merely through longevity.
Critique of household oppression supports recognition beyond a single family norm.
Women’s equal public participation contradicts compulsory traditional roles.
Freedom and equality favour inclusion, but the historical doctrine does not prescribe modern marriage categories.
The inherited household should not be treated as a universally superior form.
Women’s emancipation and reproductive ethical judgement require a conditional modern application.
Parental traditionalism should not monopolise children’s social education.
Equal personhood supports openness but no historical adoption standard is specified.
Dress customs should not constrain equal participation in public life.
Language can change through public experience without a single mandatory doctrine of identity.
Critical political learning should challenge inherited oppressive customs.
Women’s emancipation supports crossing traditional social and occupational roles.
Revolutionary democratic change need not be artificially gradual.
Open education can discuss different forms of human life without traditional censorship.
Voluntary cultural continuity is compatible with freedom, obligatory preservation is not.

axes.brief: Socialist development requires experimentation and learning; productivity cannot be separated from social consequences.
axes.counterEvidence: No source mentions AI, neural implants or embryo enhancement. Responses are labelled inferred and balance development against democratically assessed harms.

answers.rationale: Innovation should develop through public learning while harms remain democratically contestable.
Experimentation is valuable but large risks can justify trial limits.
Productive needs and damage to communities require democratic assessment.
Common health merits substantial safety investigation.
Automation can release labour or intensify domination depending on control and distribution.
Local life and material development both require consideration.
Experimental food production deserves testing rather than doctrinal acceptance or prohibition.
Healthy-person enhancement warrants caution about irreversible effects.
Technical tools cannot replace social transformation or ecological judgement.
Communities should understand environmental consequences before irreversible construction.
Free development and serious bodily risk support a conditional judgement.
Democratic health provision needs dependable evidence for varied patients.
New capacities and intergenerational risk require open collective deliberation.
Ecological uncertainty warrants adequate evidence before widespread cultivation.
Housing and transport needs matter without extinguishing preservation claims.
Irreversible harm should not be imposed without strong justification.

axes.brief: Mass self-government coexists with coordinated socialist production; rejection of national fragmentation qualifies separatist localism.
axes.counterEvidence: Internationalism and objections to nationalist fragmentation do not require a single police bureaucracy or silence local participation.

answers.rationale: Active regional institutions can sustain mass political participation.
Common planning and local agency should be reconciled rather than automatic national supremacy.
Her critique of nationalist self-determination weighs against a universal unilateral secession rule.
National plans need cooperation but bureaucratic override can destroy initiative.
Regional institutional variation can fit democratic self-government.
Local accountability counters a central coercive apparatus.
Common working-class resources require solidarity beyond wealthy regions.
Common education and regional participation should both shape curricula.
Tax autonomy is permissible only within common redistributive responsibilities.
Shared labour protections prevent regional competition at workers’ expense.
Local participants should have a real say in council organisation.
Common health guarantees can require national coordination.
Opposition to colonial dispossession supports Indigenous local institutions.
Tax competition should not undermine common social aims.
Locally confined ecological decisions warrant regional participation.
A shared emergency can justify national coordination with active local involvement.

axes.brief: Luxemburg describes social instincts and initiative developing through democratic public life, alongside a materialist recognition of natural life.
axes.counterEvidence: Democratic transformation is an account of political learning, not an empirical estimate of genetic influence on every psychological trait.

answers.rationale: She explicitly expects public social experience to transform habits and initiative.
Social education and colonial conditions matter in her developmental account, while material human capacities remain relevant; this does not establish a majority cause for country IQ differences.
Household and workplace oppression provide a social explanation of gendered conduct.
Material hardship and embodied susceptibility can both shape stress.
Participation and opportunity develop interests rather than merely reveal fixed traits.
Political learning changes risk judgements without excluding individual dispositions.
Democratic public life is expressly expected to develop social instincts and cooperation.
Shared experience nurtures concern without proving biological differences irrelevant.
Education and individual capacities can both influence attention.
Political experience is expected to reshape moral habits and judgement.
Racist and nationalist mobilisation socially produces perceptions of threat.
Her account of transformed public habits does not erase individual temperament.
Cultural formation and embodied preference remain jointly plausible.
Her account of racial oppression emphasises exploitative social relations, supporting a modest structural inference about violence rather than a demonstrated racial heritability claim.
Social learning and initiative oppose a racial destiny account of self-control.

Her critique of the capitalist classification of domestic labour as unproductive and of workplace exploitation favours social organisation over differences in productive contribution as the main explanation of pay gaps.

review.notes: Read all 240 answers against the current question wording and checked values, rationales, cited source IDs and axis distinctions. Read The Russian Revolution chapter 6 and SEP treatment of reform, revolution, colonialism and women’s emancipation; checked the SAGE scholarly source. Preserved opposition freedom alongside revolutionary socialism. Corrected Nationalism15 from a reversed value/rationale to a conditional federation judgement. Tightened country-IQ and racial-violence causal claims. The modern technology answers remain explicitly conditional applications, not attributed historical statements. All answers remain labelled inferred: these are scoped representative models, not claimed questionnaire responses or empirical measurements of adherents. Review used no target scores or similarity tuning. Similarity audit remains the catalogue coordinator’s separate step.
